At 6:29am on 7 October 2023, Mia Schem was filming a video with her friend Elia Toledano when the sound of rockets started.

They had been waiting for the sun to rise over the Negev desert in southern Israel at the Nova music festival, just 3 miles from the Israel-Gaza border.

By the end of the day, the 21-year-old described how she was shot in the arm by a Hamas militant and taken hostage into the Gaza Strip, and 378 people from the festival would be among 1,200 people killed. Israel launched a relentless two-year barrage of strikes in response, leaving 70,000 Palestinians dead in Gaza and reducing much of the enclave to rubble.

In the early days of the war, Hamas released a video of Schem in captivity, the first footage of any of the 251 hostages. The French-Israeli citizen was held in Gaza for 55 days before being released during a brief truce between Israel and Hamas.

open image in gallery Mia Schem, 21, appears in a Hamas hostage video in the days following the 7 October attacks. ( AFP/Hamas handout )

Speaking with The Independent in London, Schem has flown from her home in Shoham, a town on the outskirts of Tel Aviv in Israel.

She said she had only decided to attend the music festival on a whim. “I remember that I asked Elia, ‘Do you want to go to the Nova Festival?’ and he tell me ‘Yes, why not?’” she says.

She drove to Toledano’s house, her best friend, and they took his car to the festival site.

“I didn’t know the party was close to Gaza,” she says, because the organisers of the Nova festival tended to share the locations of the raves only a few hours before the scheduled start time.

Even if she had known that information, it would not have impacted her decision to go. “Who thought that something like that would happen,” she says.

open image in gallery Palestinian militants move towards the border fence with Israel from Khan Yunis in the southern Gaza Strip on October 7, 2023. ( AFP via Getty Images )

Once the rockets started, Schem grabbed Toledano and headed straight for his car. She believes they were one of the first few cars to leave the Nova festival site.

At this stage in the day seemingly innocuous decisions would decide whether or not you would survive the terrorist attack.

When leaving the festival site those who turned right were saved, Schem says, and those who turned left towards Tel Aviv and Jerusalem were met by Hamas.

“Me and Elia were the first people to see the terrorists,” she says. Hamas gunmen were standing at either side of the road, shooting at cars and killing passengers as they sped past. Schem thought there could have been as many as 40 gunmen in the road.

Schem floored it through the roadblock but says their car was riddled with bullets.

open image in gallery Abandoned vehicles at the site of the 7 October attack on the Nova music festival in the Negev desert in southern Israel. ( AFP via Getty Images )

The vehicle rolled twice, and Toledano and Schem were forced to escape out of the vehicle’s windows, as the doors were jammed. They tried to hide next to the car.

Toledano grabbed her phone and began calling the emergency services, but the messages that came back were grim.

“They tell us on the phone, ‘You need to hide. We can’t help you,’” Schem says, “Nobody came to save us.”

When she was hiding on the ground, she was shot in the arm by a Hamas terrorist: “ They shot me from point-blank range.”

Both Schem and Toledano were abducted and taken into Gaza. Only one of them would return alive.

The body of Elia Toledano would be eventually retrieved by the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) from the Gaza Strip in late 2023.

There was a “high probability” that his cause of death was due to an Israeli airstrike, according to an IDF investigation.

open image in gallery Palestinian militants transport a reportedly captured Israeli woman by motorcycle, in Khan Yunis in the southern Gaza Strip. ( AFP via Getty Images )

When describing her time in Hamas captivity in Gaza, Schem is unequivocal. She was treated like an “animal in a cage,” she recounts.

She believes the only reason she was saved from being raped was because she was being kept in the home of her captor.

“He didn’t touch me, but the reason was because his wife and children were behind the door,” Schem adds.

She said her captor’s wife would mistreat Schem because she resented the fact that she was in the same room as her husband: “She didn’t give me water or food.”

Five days before she was released, Schem says she was taken down into the tunnels beneath Gaza where she first encountered other hostages.Five women were also being held there.

Schem has told Israeli television that this was the hardest time of her captivity because of the hopelessness of the hostages she met down there.

open image in gallery Visitors walk among burnt out cars and tents at the Nova Music Festival Exhibition in Berlin, Germany. ( Getty Images )

Schem was in London to recount her story to an audience at the Nova Exhibition. The exhibition recreates the music festival with real wreckage brought over from Israel. “ It's a miracle that I'm here.” she says, “and if God saved me, I never give up.”

The exhibition has been travelling around the world, and London is the 10th city it has visited so far. Now, plans are underway for the exhibition to travel to Paris, Budapest and Prague in the future.

When the exhibition travelled to New York, hundreds of people gathered in Lower Manhattan to protest against Israel’s conduct since October 7th, with some accusing the show of being political propaganda.

News.title: England win gives Borthwick breathing space after late try controversy
News.content:
And in doing so he may have just saved Borthwick’s job.

The Rugby Football Union, following its review into England’s Six Nations campaign that yielded just one victory, had publicly offered its backing to its head coach through to the World Cup. But in reality, there are no guarantees. It needed evidence of England’s progress.

Two wins from three rounds of the Nations Championship is likely to convince RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney to back his man. But Borthwick will know that nothing can be taken for granted.

Four years ago, Eddie Jones, facing similar scrutiny from his employers, looked to have salvaged his job by winning the last two matches in a three-Test summer tour of Australia. But it did still not save him from the sack the following November.

Still. There was enough character and attacking prowess to convince the RFU that, despite the flaws in this display, the team are on the right track again.

It was still far from an 80-minute performance, but this was England’s first away victory in a year, in a hostile environment and after all the challenges, both physical and mental, the players have faced in travelling to three continents over three weeks – clocking up more than 25,000 miles – at the end of a long season.

England wobbled alarmingly earlier in the second half but remarkably found the resilience to drag themselves back into the game just as it looked like it was slipping from their grasp. That is clear evidence of players playing for their coach and each other.

Discipline, however, remains a major problem for Borthwick’s England. They had been cruising to what would looked to have been a statement victory at half-time following tries by Tommy Freeman and two by Ben Earl, in what had been their finest half of rugby this year.

And yet, once again indiscipline undermined their efforts. Remarkably, they were shown four yellow cards – Jack van Poortvliet, Alex Coles, Pollock (to more booing) and Emmanuel Iyogun – in the second half to take their total to 14 in their last 10 Tests, and at one stage were down to 12 men but, significantly, this time it did not prove fatal.

News.title: Tuchel learns lesson as England clinch third place in 10-goal thriller
News.content:
Neither England nor France wanted to be playing this game in Miami, but they can have no complaints about the nature of their semi-final defeats.

Tournament favourites France were comprehensively outplayed by Spain, with their feted front four of Kylian Mbappe, Ousmane Dembele, Bradley Barcola and Michael Olise all turning in below-par performances.

England’s defeat by Argentina was perhaps not as much of a surprise, but the nature of Thomas Tuchel’s team’s second-half collapse was just as alarming as France’s no-show.

England’s manager was fiercely criticised for replacing Anthony Gordon with Ezri Konsa and switching to a back five in the 72nd minute, but Tuchel has since defended his decisions.

“If you are asking if I regret my decisions, if this is the question, then I say no. I don’t regret my ‌decisions because I ‌felt that we became ⁠too passive,” said Tuchel.

“I took several decisions, trusting my instinct, my intuition, my experience, trusting my competitiveness, and I took the decision in order to help the team and get the result.

“I would regret if I didn’t help. I would regret ⁠if we didn’t react, but I have no regrets over the decision itself.”

Quite how strong Didier Deschamps and Tuchel decide to go with their teams is anyone’s guess. There has been some suggestion that Mbappe will start to give him the chance to beat Lionel Messi to the Golden Boot.

Some of England’s regular starters, such as Declan Rice, look physically spent, so there could be some rotation, and even a chance for players such as Kobbie Mainoo who has not played a minute of football at the tournament.

The third/fourth-place play-off has been rebranded as the “Bronze Final” for this tournament, and Tuchel was keen to point out that finishing third would be England’s best World Cup result since 1966. They lost this fixture against Belgium in 2018, but the way that game has been widely forgotten speaks volumes.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Scotland fight back to claim victory against Fiji in Nations Championship
News.content:
A barrelling Schoeman finished an initial break by match captain Stafford McDowall, then Dobie burrowed over beside the posts in the 61st minute to put Scotland in front for the first time in 40 minutes.

Scotland glossed up the scoreline with two more tries in the last six minutes by Cummings and Dobie again to send home a crowd of 55,000 happy.

“I thought our bench did really well,” Townsend told the BBC. “Something I’ve learned over the last 12 months, the bench can help you change momentum. The players can come up with solutions themselves but the bench can give you energy and solutions but also bravery. We’re a team that will back our decisions and that put real pressure on Fiji.

“I felt [Fiji] picked their strongest side today and it took a lot of work for us to break them down but also it took a really good defensive performance,” Townsend added. “Fiji didn’t really break us that often [and] in that final quarter the guys were outstanding. We’ll take a few positives from that.”

Fiji had never beaten Scotland at Murrayfield but would have sensed the chance of making history by half-time. The Fijians were tough and clinical in a huge turnaround from last weekend when they were humiliated by England 73-8 in Liverpool.

News.title: Hometown hero Tommy Fleetwood facing tough ask to end 57 years of Open hurt
News.content:
Never mind Bryson DeChambeau stomping around in the rough as he improved his lie, for so long this Open Saturday turned into Tommy Fleetwood walking in his Royal Birkdale wonderland as he enhanced the mood of seemingly everyone in attendance.

Alas, the fun could not last and, even though he still has a chance of becoming England’s first Open winner on English soil since 1969, that finish looked costly. Fifty-seven years of hurt and all that...

On five under, Fleetwood is in a tie for ninth, five off the lead held by Sam Burns, the American who, after a 65, is two clear of New Zealander Ryan Fox and South Korean Kim Si-woo. DeChambeau is alongside Swede Ludvig Aberg, in a tie for sixth on six under, after a 69.

He was heckled on the 18th because of the two-shot penalty he received on Friday night for “inadvertently improving his lie” on the fifth. “You’re a cheat, Bryson,” the fan shouted.

It was a sour point that was in no way in keeping with the mood of this Saturday that had been overwhelmingly positive. With Fleetwood as the focus, of course.

The enormous crowd cheered and sang and backed their fellow Merseysider all the way as Fleetwood launched his charge into contention at this Southport links which he would once sneak on as a child. His playing partner, Jon Rahm, was taken aback by the level of support.

“The best way I can explain it, it was so intense that, without meaning any disrespect I’m glad England didn’t win the semi-final [of the World Cup] because I would have been having a heck of a three days with the fans if they had been playing Spain in tomorrow’s final,” Rahm said.

News.title: Sloppy Springboks still strong enough to pulverise Wales
News.content:
If one image summed up South Africa’s complete control, it was in the 12th minute when Wales had a scrum on their own five-metre line. When the Springbok shove came, the Welsh pack went backwards like they were on roller-skates. The poor Welsh front row are going to have to check under their beds for snarling Springboks props for quite a few sleepless nights to come.

Wales’ best period of the game came just after the Springboks’ fourth try when they had three line-outs and took three tap penalties deep inside the South Africa 22. It amounted to absolutely nothing.

You can point fingers at head coach Steve Tandy’s selections and preparation if you wish, but there was little he could have done to change the result. It was only the manner of their hammering, he could have potentially affected.

Wales are not alone in this. Scotland and England may have posed a few more problems but they were still dispatched with ease. South Africa are truly in a league of their own, although New Zealand’s resurgence under Dave Rennie should at least provide a serious level of competition that the British mainland failed to provide.

In truth the best thing that Tandy could do is burn the tapes and hope that this is consigned to the deepest recesses of their collective memory. Tighthead Dillon Lewis especially may need one of those Men in Black memory wipers.

If you squinted hard enough, there were a couple of positives: the maul defence and high-ball contest. They were at least competitive. Aaron Wainwright had the unenviable job of packing down at the back of a retreating Welsh scrum but did a heroic job in the circumstances. Jac Morgan, too, was bravery personified in attacking the breakdown with the ferocity of the Springboks clean-out operation.

But in the infrequent periods when South Africa got on a roll without knocking on, there was precious little Wales could do to stop the green wave. The first try was a case in point. Emanating from a loose kick from Tomos Williams, full-back Aphelele Fassi broke the first line of Wales’ defence and then they kept coming through Cobus Wiese, Damien de Allende before Jasper Wiese accelerated through Morgan’s tackle and over the line.

News.title: Santos impresses in first Man Utd appearance but cannot prevent defeat by Wrexham
News.content:
United were without the players who have featured at this summer’s World Cup – including new signing Youri Tielemans – as well as Benjamin Sesko, but Michael Carrick put out a strong starting XI in front of 20,000 spectators in the Finnish capital.

Santos, who became United’s first summer signing when he joined from Chelsea at the start of the week for an initial £48m, took his place at the base of midfield alongside Mason Mount.

Speaking just before the match, Michael Carrick had praised the 22-year-old’s attitude, saying: “He’s settled in really well, he’s a fantastic character. He’s buzzing to be here, you can see that.”

The Brazilian’s first involvement was to clear the ball away after Tom Heaton failed to gather under pressure from Smith seconds into the game.

Santos was left on his backside by Lewis O’Brien eight minutes in but the chance came to nothing for Wrexham as the flag went up. More encouraging was his sliding block on O’Brien moments later and he soon settled in, showing a good range of passing and winning several duels in a busy display.

However, Phil Parkinson’s side, who played their first pre-season friendly against Wisla Krakow in Poland last weekend, were looking brighter and threatened again when Bailey Cadamarteri nicked the ball off Ayden Heaven on the edge of the box before the defender recovered.

United’s first chance was a Joshua Zirkzee shot that fizzed wide in the 24th minute and they almost went ahead when Smith tried to clear a cornerm but instead sent a header on to his own crossbar in the 36th minute.

News.title: Russell fighting ‘with one hand behind my back’ as Antonelli takes Belgium GP pole
News.content:
Russell and Mercedes are not clueless about his woes. Russell believes he is losing the bulk of the time on the straights, though Toto Wolff, the team principal, conceded that some time is also being lost in the corners. They are both, however, struggling to explain why he is haemorrhaging time in the flat-out sections of a track that is replete with them. It was the same at Silverstone, when Russell repeatedly bemoaned his power deficit to Antonelli and the other Mercedes-powered cars.

Heading into this weekend, Russell believed that these issues were down to Antonelli’s driving style leading to better battery deployment on the straights. “That’s what we thought coming out of Silverstone. We thought it was in the driving style and technique, but we have finally concluded it’s not. We have changed everything... it’s frustrating,” he said.

“So we keep going through this process of ‘Oh, we think it’s this’. We change it. ‘Oh, it’s not this, maybe it’s the driving style’. I thought it was the driving style. Honestly, I came into this weekend and said on Thursday, ‘I think it’s the driving style’. Changed the driving style, and it’s not the driving style.”

“Anything can happen [in the race]. But as I said, the truth is battling against my team-mate, who is such an incredible driver, doing such a great job at the moment, in the best of times, is a tall order.

Sports.title: How long is half-time in the World Cup final?
Sports.content:
PRESS PAUSE How long is half-time in the World Cup final?

FOR the first time in World Cup history, there will be a Super Bowl-style half-time show.

Argentina and Spain are set to clash for the right to call themselves world champions in 2026.



Lionel Messi and Co are looking to become the first side in 60 years to win the World Cup in consecutive tournaments, following their triumph in 2022.

However, they face a Spanish side who won Euro 2024, and have won eight consecutive knockout games across the Euros and World Cup.



But in the midst of what promises to be a must-see battle in New York, there will be an extended half-time.



SunSport can reveal how long half-time in the World Cup final is.

How long is half-time in the World Cup final?

The World Cup final will have a slightly longer half-time than usual.

The half-time interval is expected to last for up to 25 minutes, 10 minutes longer than the normal 15 minute interval.

The break is extended to accommodate for a Super Bowl-style half-time show, in which there will be an 11-minute concert.



Coldplay front-man Chris Martin will curate the headline show, and is set to be joined by Justin Beiber, Madonna, Shakira, Gustavo Dudamel and BTS.

ITV and BBC will be broadcasting the show as part of their World Cup final coverage.

Sports.title: When is World Cup 2026 closing ceremony and who is performing?
Sports.content:
FIFA is throwing a star-studded send-off for the biggest World Cup in history, ahead of the first kick of the ball in the final.

There will also be a big-budget half-time show. Here’s everything that has been confirmed so far.



When is the World Cup 2026 closing ceremony?

The closing ceremony will be held at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey, just outside New York, ahead of the final on Sunday, July 19, 2026.

Fifa‘s official media release states the ceremony starts at 6.30pm (1.30pm ET), 90 minutes before kick-off.



Fans with tickets can get into the stadium from 11am local time, four hours before the match.

Fifa said supporters inside the ground will enjoy “a full suite of experiences… including exclusive activations, rewards and additional pre-match entertainment.”



The show will celebrate the 48 competing teams’ journey across the tournament’s three host countries and 16 host cities.

Fifa chief operating officer Heimo Schirgi said: “Echoing the spirit of the opening ceremonies, which welcomed the world to the greatest stage in Canada, Mexico and the United States, the closing ceremony will bring the Fifa World Cup 2026 full circle through music, culture and football, before we kick off the highly anticipated match that will crown the champions of this groundbreaking tournament.”

Who is performing at the closing ceremony?

Tom Cruise is set for a special appearance, following his role in the closing ceremony of the Paris Olympics, where he performed a spectacular multi-stage stunt to symbolically pass the Olympic flag to the 2028 host city, Los Angeles.

He was also spotted earlier in the tournament taking in USA and Paraguay in LA on June 12.



Tom will be joined by stars including Nicole Scherzinger and IShowSpeed.

Robbie Williams will also be on hand to belt out his Fifa football anthem ‘Desire‘ with Italian pop star Laura Pausini

Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony Award winner Jennifer Hudson will perform the US national anthem ahead of the final.

Fifa says more artists and special guests could be announced in the coming days.

What is the World Cup final half-time show?

A separate Super Bowl style half-time show will run during the final’s mid-match interval, curated by Coldplay’s Chris Martin.



It is the first time a World Cup final has featured a half-time performance.

The musical segment itself lasts around 11 minutes, but the full halftime interval is expected to stretch to somewhere between 20 and 30 minutes to allow for the stage to be built and cleared, well beyond the usual 15-minute break.

Law 7 of the Laws of the Game states that halftime should not exceed 15 minutes, though it also allows competition organisers to set the duration and permits changes with the referee’s agreement.

The elite list of co-headliners for the half-time show are Justin Bieber, Madonna, Shakira, and South Korean boyband BTS.



The incredible line-up will also feature performances from Burna Boy, Venezuelan conductor Gustavo Dudamel, and the PS22 Chorus – a choir of school children from Staten Island – joined by Coldplay.

There will also be appearances from characters from Sesame Street and The Muppets.

The performance supports the Fifa Global Citizen Education Fund, which is aiming to raise $100million (£75million) to expand access to education and football for children worldwide, with a dollar from every match ticket sold going towards the fund.

How can I watch it in the UK?

The World Cup final is being shown on both BBC One and ITV1.

At the time of writing, it is unclear whether the broadcasters will be showing the full closing ceremony, or just the highlights.



Coverage is set to begin on ITV at 6.45pm, while on the BBC it starts from 7pm.

There is a chance both broadcasters may offer a live stream of the pre-match ceremony via their streaming services, though this is not yet confirmed.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

ITV bosses told The Sun they will broadcast the half-time show in full alongside the usual football analysis.

A BBC spokesperson said: “Plans for the final will be announced in due course.”

ENGLAND’S freestyle football world champion, Lia Lewis, has got engaged while on holiday in the Maldives.

The 29-year-old, who won gold back in 2021, was surprised with a proposal from Nolan Cacheux, also a fellow freestyle football professional like herself.

The pair got engaged at Kandima in the Maldives, a resort Lewis has been to before on her travels.



She returned two years after her initial visit to be a part of the resort’s Summer Kamp 2026 programme, leading freestyle football workshops for guests during the FIFA World Cup season.



Lewis actually made it out to the World Cup, posting from the pitch ahead of the France v Spain semi-final.

She regularly delights her 1.4 million followers on Instagram with her insane skills in jaw-dropping locations.

Kandima has increasingly become a go-to destination for people inside the world of football.



Mario Balotelli paid a visit to the island at the beginning of the year and even took a coaching session with kids on the resort’s full size pitch.

But he is far from the only pro to make his way to the slice of paradise.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso ‘deems Chelsea star untouchable amid major transfer interest from rival’ despite £117m Morgan Rogers arrival
Sports.content:
CHELSEA star Joao Pedro is reportedly untouchable and will therefore NOT join Barcelona.

The Brazilian was sounded out to be a potential replacement for Robert Lewandowski in Catalonia but Chelsea chiefs are understood to have closed the door on any deal.



Despite Spanish reports suggesting the star would “welcome” a move to the Blaugrana, according to Diario Sport, the door is well and truly closed.

He has been declared untouchable and Chelsea have no intention of listening to offers from anyone.



New gaffer Xabi Alonso appears to view him as a key figure in his project, following Pedro‘s productive debut campaign at Stamford Bridge.

He scored 15 goals in 35 Premier League appearances as well as providing 8 assists.

He was arguably one of few shining lights in a dark season for the West London club, as they finished a lowly tenth in the Premier League, having had three different managers.

And as a result, he’s been put on the untouchable list, along with young star Josh Acheampong.

Following BlueCo’s appointment of Alonso as manager, as opposed to head coach, it’s been suggested that the new gaffer will have more of a say on the squad than any of his predecessors.

And it seems to have started that way, Chelsea’s previous interest in Granit Xhaka was a clear demonstration of their commitment to the new manager, despite Sunderland blocking the move.

Xhaka was Alonso’s captain at Bayer Leverkusen as the Spaniard delivered a first ever Bundesliga title to the BayArena.

Additionally, the breaking Morgan Rogers news yesterday was a hell of a statement by the Blues.

They have agreed a huge deal worth £117million with Aston Villa to bring the midfielder to the Bridge, making him the most expensive British player ever.

The attacker has agreed a six-year contract at Stamford Bridge – with SunSport having first reported the Blues’ interest in July 2025.

Rogers is said to have been impressed by Alonso‘s vision for the club.

Sports.title: England World Cup hero Djed Spence ‘truly wants to leave Tottenham for shock foreign transfer’
Sports.content:
DJED SPENCE wants to leave Tottenham for Inter Milan, according to reports in Italy.

The England full-back impressed at the World Cup as the Three Lions achieved a podium finish.



Spence’s club future remains unclear, however, amid stiff competition for places at Spurs.

Andrew Robertson‘s arrival in addition to Destiny Udogie means that left-back will be a difficult spot fill.



And Pedro Porro’s pre-World Cup contract extension suggests that he will be the main man at right-back.

According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Inter want to sign Spence as their replacement for Real Madrid-bound Denzel Dumfries.



They add that Spence “truly wants” the move – but that it will depend on how much Tottenham demand.

Inter are said to be willing to fork out around £30million on the 25-year-old.

Should Spurs ask for more following Spence’s impressive World Cup, Inter may struggle to complete a deal.

Spence, who signed for Tottenham four years ago today, is under contract with the North Londoners for another three years, with the option for a further season.



WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS

Earlier this month, The Athletic reported that Everton are also interested in Spence.

David Moyes‘ side are looking for a long-term replacement for stalwart Seamus Coleman.

Spence joined Tottenham from Middlesbrough in 2022 following a successful loan at Nottingham Forest.

The defender barely got a look in early on his Spurs career, with then-boss Antonio Conte damningly calling him a “club signing”.



Underwhelming loans at Rennes and Leeds followed, before a more productive stint with Italian side Genoa.

In the summer of 2024, Spence managed to earn a place in Ange Postecoglou‘s plans for the following season.

And following a slew of first team injuries that winter, he was finally granted a chance to show what he could do.

Spence has played 85 times for Tottenham in total, including a late cameo in their victorious Europa League final in 2025.

He has also earned 14 England caps, featuring in all eight of their matches at this summer’s World Cup.

Sports.title: England stars land back home after 10-hour flight following World Cup third-place thriller win over France
Sports.content:
ENGLAND stars have landed back home after their harrowing World Cup exit at the hands of Argentina.

They lifted off from Miami on Saturday night and touched down in Birmingham after seven weeks on the road together.



The Three Lions bowed out of the tournament in Miami with a third-place – their best finish since triumphing in 1966.

The ten-goal thriller against France was hailed as one of the maddest World Cup games ever.



But it’s the heartbreaking 2-1 loss to Argentina on Wednesday night that everyone will remember.

The Atlanta defeat had them packing their bags earlier than expected with the holders set to face Spain in the final this evening.

On the night, Anthony Gordon lifted the hopes of the nation in the 55th minute as crowds erupted with celebrations.

But it was not meant to be as England dropped back and eventually Chelsea’s Enzo Fernandez found the back of the net.



Hanging on by the scruff of their necks, Lautaro Martinez put the nail in the coffin to send Argentina to New Jersey.

Since then, Thomas Tuchel has come under fire as players and fans criticise his choice of subsitutes when Gordon took the lead.

WORLD CUP 2026 FREE BETS AND SIGN UP OFFERS



But it seems as the FA and the England stars have backed him until at least Euro 2028, when England co-host with Scotland, Wales, and Republic of Ireland.

As England took the stage for the final time on Saturday night.



Fans were not expecting much from what is usually one of the worst games of the tournament.

But within three minutes, Declan Rice had burst out the gates and handed England the lead.

Ezri Konsa doubled it and fans were left wondering what could have been as Bukayo Saka bagged two before the break.

Assistant coach Anthony Barry delivered a tearjerking half-time interview as he roused the spirits of fans watching back home.

The tides turned in the second-half as Kylian Mbappe took the lead in the race for the Golden Boot.



Before long, Bradley Barcola and another from Mbappe threatened to comeback.

And despite a late goal from Ousmane Dembele, Saka completed his hat-trick and Jude Bellingham characteristically scored in the depths of injury time.

Sports.title: Heartbreaking reason Spain star Lamine Yamal's dad won't attend World Cup final
Sports.content:
Heartbreaking reason Spain star Lamine Yamal's dad won't attend World Cup final

Lamine Yamal is looking to outgun Lionel Messi in the World Cup final as Spain collide with Argentina for the biggest prize in football

View 2 Images Lamine Yamal with his dad Mounir Nasraoui after winning Euro 2024 with Spain

Lamine Yamal's father will not attend the World Cup final in person - as he hasn't been able to end any match all tournament.

‌



Mounir Nasraoui has revealed he did not feel fit to travel this summer due to his health. It means Nasraoui is set to cheer on the 19-year-old Barcelona superstar from home.

‌



He explained: "I'm an epileptic. I have to take a lot of medication every day, and I can have an epilepsy seizure.

‌



"I could be here, right now, under the effects of stress or emotion, and have a seizure without realising it. So you always have to think things through carefully.

"Before traveling, you have to think about me, about him, and about all the people around us, you know? I might end up causing problems. So it's better to stay home and watch all this from here."

Spain and Argentina World Cup final training plans rocked by electrical thunderstorms READ MORE :

Spain star Aymeric Laporte calls out Argentina over England World Cup antics READ MORE :

Around a month after Yamal's last major tournament, Euro 2024 - which he won, dad Mounir was stabbed in a parking lot. The authorities arrested four people in connection with the incident.

‌



He remains very close to his family despite his superstardom. His brother Keyne, who is three years old, has been one of the heroes of this World Cup due to his celebrations in the stands.

"I come from an apartment where the kitchen and the bedroom were the same space," Yamal recently stated, citing his humble beginnings.

"I see my mother happy, I see that my brother can have the childhood I would have liked to have, and that's what makes me happiest."

‌



View 2 Images Mounir Nasraoui, the father of Lamine Yamal, suffers with epilepsy

Fatima, Yamal's paternal grandmother, left Morocco on a bus that she wasn't legally allowed to board. She would work shifts just so her son could join before he ended up having Yamal as a teenager.

Now that 19-year-old is about to walk out on the biggest stage of all. While Yamal's parents split when he was three, his football career took off soon after.

‌



He joined Barcelona's youth ranks at seven, though he was actually scouted at the age of seven and at the age of 15, he made his big breakthrough into the first-team.

In doing so, he became the youngest player to make their debut for the Catalan giants since way back in 1922.

Yamal has scored just one goal at this World Cup but after shaking off a thigh issue, he is expected to start against Argentina as he looks to add a second international trophy to his cabinet.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's numbers do not do justice to his genius - but second World Cup will
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's numbers do not do justice to his genius - but second World Cup will

Gianni Infantino said the tournament would not have been 'an incredible success without Donald Trump' but it is the world's greatest player who has made it truly compelling

View 4 Images Lionel Messi has scored eight goals at World Cup 2026 (Image: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images)

In theory, it was his wrong foot - as if he has got a wrong foot. Across the edge of England’s six-yard box was a cordon of tall defenders. But he still picked out Lautaro Martinez. In the added minutes of a World Cup semi-final that can scramble the coolest head, he picked out Martinez and invited him to send Argentina to the final.

‌



When all is said and done about England’s capitulation in Atlanta last Wednesday, it was another chapter in the epic, footballing tale being written by Lionel Messi. And should he lead Argentina to back-to-back World Cup triumphs, the only unpalatable sight in New Jersey will be of Gianni Infantino and Donald Trump sharing the stage with the greatest footballer of all time.

‌



Harry Kane's sad admission to England teammates spotted by lip reader after France win READ MORE :

Argentina stars taunted England from team bus after World Cup win as cutting message revealed READ MORE :

Their double act in New York ahead of tonight’s final between Argentina and Spain was nauseous on a predictably grand scale. Sorry, it is no double act. It is puppeteer and puppet. Jonny, as Trump calls him, says what Trump wants him to say.

‌



And on this occasion, Jonny said: “You don’t need people to compliment you, Mr President, but this World Cup would not have been such an incredible success without you.” No, he does need people to compliment him, and Infantino has been happy to oblige. He invented FIFA’S Peace Prize for him, for goodness sake.

Whether or not World Cup 2026 has been ‘an incredible success’ or not is, as usual, a subjective matter. But to be scrupulously fair, even the most sceptical must have enjoyed it to some extent.

The 48-team format did not produce as many mismatches and dead rubbers as we might have thought.

‌



View 4 Images Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino will present the World Cup trophy to the winners in New Jersey (Image: Getty)

It gave us some nice stories, the Cape Verde journey being the standard-bearer for an expanded competition. And there has been some enthralling football in the knockout stages.

Few would complain about having an extra knockout stage. Hands up, I started the World Cup vehemently opposed to a 48-team event … now, a 64-team event would not bother me.

‌



The breadth and gaiety of the competing nations and their supporters have been sights to behold and the venues have, in the main, looked sensational. There is, though, a lengthy snag list, headed by the exorbitant cost of getting into games and being there.

It will go down as the most-attended World Cup but it is still THE rip-off World Cup. And then there was the banning of Somalian referee Omar Artan, the poor treatment of the Iranian national team and the lifting of Folarin Balogun’s suspension after the Trump intervention.

View 4 Images Lautaro Martinez headed Lionel Messi's cross home to end England's hopes of winning the World Cup (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



“Jonny made yet another of his good decisions,” Trump said on Friday. And then there was the hydration-break system, a running sore through the four and a half weeks of competition.

But in the end, FIFA - and Infantino - will get away with fundamentally changing the format of a football match. They will get away with it because the football has been largely compelling.

And nothing has been more compelling than Messi, at the age of 39, redefining his greatness. Here are some stats from this World Cup.

‌



Most shots - 34 (Messi). Most chances created - 25 (Messi). Most take-ons completed - 25 (Messi). Most accurate crosses - 19 (Messi). Most through balls - 15 (Messi). Most goal involvements - 12 (Messi). Most big chances created - 8 (Messi). Most goals - 10 (Mbappe, Messi second with 8).

View 4 Images Lionel Messi inspired Argentina to their World Cup win in Qatar (Image: Getty Images)

They are remarkable numbers but those of us who have watched Messi for over two decades know that numbers do not even come close to doing justice to his genius. Argentina’s antics during and after the semi-final win were not to everyone’s taste. There will be little support for them in England.

‌



But to see Messi inspire his nation was a sight to behold in Qatar in 2022, and is even more so four years later. So, when Infantino tells Trump this World Cup would not have been such an incredible success without him, he is fundamentally wrong.

This World Cup would not have been such an incredible success - if that is what you think it is - without Lionel Messi. And it will be hard to begrudge him a remarkable final act.

Sports.content:
BBC's Joe Hart in bizarre video before World Cup final with pundit DRENCHED in monsoon weather

Ex-England goalkeeper Joe Hart filmed a bizarre video on Saturday as he was caught up in torrential rain before working on the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina

Joe Hart lost his shoes and was left drenched after torrential rain hit New York ahead of the World Cup final.

‌



Former Manchester City and England goalkeeper Hart took to Instagram after a walk in The Big Apple turned into an underwater scene when pouring rain caused chaos in the United States on Saturday. Hart, who has been a familiar face during BBC's World Cup coverage this summer, has travelled out to the US alongside the likes of Wayne Rooney and Micah Richards to work as a pundit for Sunday's final.

‌



But while he was having a chilled walk, torrential rain caused Hart to get drenched. In a video on his Instagram story, the 39-year-old said: "The weather is absolutely banging here, shoes are off, trainers are ruined, COME ON!"

‌



The downpour forced Hart to walk barefoot as he was pictured with his shoes instead in his hands. As well as that, his white t-shirt was sodden and his sunglasses were nowhere to be seen on his head.

Hart then decided to pan the camera round to show the puddles of rain on the road with a car trying to make its way through the flash flood. Meanwhile, people with umbrellas ran to shelter and tried to get from the rain.

Real reason Argentina President won't attend World Cup final with Donald Trump READ MORE :

It's not the first time Hart has surrounded himself with water in recent days, after he joined ex-Manchester United forward Rooney in rowing the River Hudson in New York. Rooney agreed to row if Norway reached the quarter-final after the Scandinavian nation performed the infamous Viking Row celebration at the World Cup.

‌



Although Rooney initially suggested he would row the River Mersey, he changed to the River Hudson instead upon arriving into New York for the final week of the tournament. And as Norway beat Brazil to progress to the last eight, Rooney kept to his wish as he was captured on the Hudson rowing along with Hart and Richards.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Hart, Richards and Rooney are poised to be part of the BBC punditry team working on Sunday's World Cup final between Spain and Argentina at the MetLife Stadium.

‌



Luis de la Fuente's Spain are hoping to win the tournament for the second time and the first time in 16 years, while Lionel Scaloni's Argentina are hoping to go back-to-back after running out on top four years ago in Qatar.

Spain progressed through to the showpiece final following a 2-0 win against France on Tuesday, while Argentina came from behind to beat England 2-1 and get to their third final in four tournaments.

Sports.title: Spain star calls out Donald Trump and confirms if he'll shake his hand at World Cup final
Sports.content:
Spain star calls out Donald Trump and confirms if he'll shake his hand at World Cup final

Spain striker Borja Iglesias has confirmed whether he will shake hands with Donald Trump at the 2026 World Cup final, having made his personal feelings towards the US President very clear

View 2 Images Borja Iglesias of Spain has spoken about the prospect of meeting Donald Trump (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

Spain star Borja Iglesias has called out Donald Trump for ‘struggling with fundamental values’ but has vowed to reluctantly shake the US President’s hand. The MetLife Stadium in New Jersey will host the final on Sunday evening, where Spain and Argentina will go head-to-head for the honour of being crowned world champions.

‌



Trump is expected to be in attendance for the match, having not previously attended a single game throughout the tournament so far. The US President is expected to hand over the trophy to the winning team on Sunday night.

‌



Spain won the World Cup in 2010 and are bidding to win the tournament for the second time on Sunday, but Iglesias has opened up on the mixed emotions he’s feeling about the prospect of meeting Trump.

‌



Real reason Argentina President won't attend World Cup final with Donald Trump READ MORE :

"There's a protocol and a commitment to fulfill out of politeness, even though what my gut tells me to do differs from what I should do," he said.

"I like people who fight for progress and for fundamental values to be upheld, and I think Trump struggles with that."

The striker has now provided additional insight into that potential meeting, but admitted he will shake hands with the President.

‌



"I don't want to go to prison,” Iglesias told Spanish press. "I hope to greet him at a time when we are all very happy, and that it passes very quickly and I can forget about it.

"I don't think this is the time to create controversy. People know perfectly well what I think. I would love to do many things, but the reality is that even if people think I am all-powerful, I don't have that much power to tackle certain things."

View 2 Images US President Donald Trump will attend the World Cup final (Image: Saul Loeb/Pool AFP via AP)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Iglesias has been used sparingly at this summer's tournament but has not been afraid to voice his opinion over several on-field issues in recent years.

He has consistently addressed the subject of homophobia and supported pro-Palestine protests. The striker also criticised former Spanish FA boss Luis Rubiales after he was convicted of sexual assault for kissing a player following the Women's World Cup final three years ago.

‌



Iglesias' remarks follow Spanish icon Joan Capdevila publicly appealing to Trump for assistance after being refused a visa to attend the final.

The 2010 World Cup winner suggested he was denied entry after playing in a game in Iran, writing: "I NEED HELP. They just told me that I can't travel to the final with my kids because my ESTA has been denied.

"Can anyone help me with this? You have no idea how excited I was to be there with all my 2010 teammates and this team to cheer them on.

Article continues below

"I can't believe they're not letting me into the USA... and that I'll miss a moment like this with my kids who love soccer so much. If anyone knows how to fix this, I'll be grateful to you for life."

Sports.content:
We have a busy day’s racing on Sunday with action from Newton Abbot and Chantilly, live on Sky Sports Racing...

12.58 Chantilly - Tokaido faces King Of Cloughan and Beibhinn

A classy field of three head to post for this Group Two Prix Robert Papin at Chantilly.

Amy Murphy saddles Tokaido who recorded a third success on his fourth outing when comfortably claiming the Group Three Prix du Bois under Tony Piccone. That was his first try at six-furlongs and his connections are expecting him to handle this step up in class.

Joseph O'Brien is double handed with King Of Cloughan the pick. A son of St Mark's Basilica, he built on his first couple of starts to take the Windsor Castle Stakes at the Royal meeting. Only on top late on, he will appreciate a decent pace here under new rider Pierre-Charles Boudot.

Beibhinn landed a Listowel maiden on her second start before an excellent third in this grade at the Curragh so cannot be discounted.

4.35 Chantily - Exciting Erdenali bids to remain unbeaten

Erdenali looks to extend his winning run in an excellent Group Three Prix Messidor at 4.35pm.

Francis-Henri Graffard's gelding is unbeaten in all three starts having burst onto the scene at Saint-Cloud back in March. He takes another step up the ladder here but could prove equal to the test and remains a highly promising prospect.

Christopher Ferland's Silius is a solid yardstick who has claimed silver on his last two starts at this level so must be feared if in similar spirits.

Dark Trooper and Familly complete the shortlist.

5.22 Newton Abbot - Prolific pair No More No and Edgewell clash

In-form duo No More No and Edgewell lock horns in this closing Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Handicap Chase at Newton Abbot.

Lawney Hill's No More No returned from a layoff to make it two wins from two starts over fences and he makes appeal off a three-pound higher mark. Obviously not the easiest to train, he has been given time to recover from that outing.

Edgewell arrives in red-hot form having scored over this course and distance in June before claiming a Worcester handicap in game fashion last month. He enjoys quick ground and can give another bold showing.

The Grace Harris-trained My Girl Katie has won over this trip and track and cannot be ruled out.

Sports.title: England claim third at World Cup with win in 10-goal thriller over France
Sports.content:
Bukayo Saka’s hat-trick helped England to a remarkable 6-4 bronze medal win over France in Miami to achieve their best World Cup finish since 1966.

England were incredibly 4-0 up at half-time through Declan Rice's opener, Ezri Konsa's header and Saka's double, as Thomas Tuchel's side took advantage of an uninterested France - but they nearly blew their four-goal lead in the second half.

The two-time World Cup winners woke up after half-time to threaten a sensational comeback through Kylian Mbappe's double - which saw him become the World Cup's all-time leading scorer (22 goals) - and substitute Bradley Barcola's strike.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Tuchel hits back at the negativity around England following their World Cup semi-final exit to Argentina saying it felt like they had gone out of the group stges without a win...

Michael Olise missed two glorious chances to equalise before Djed Spence won a late penalty from Malo Gusto's challenge, allowing Saka to score from the spot to complete his hat-trick in the 87th minute.

Yet there was still more drama to come as substitute Ousmane Dembele scored a 96th-minute goal to give France hope of avoiding defeat in Didier Deschamps' last game in charge.

But two minutes later, substitute Jude Bellingham struck with the 10th goal of the game to set the record for the most goals by an England player at a major tournament with seven and secure the Three Lions' third-place finish.

Image: Bukayo Saka hit a hat-trick as England beat France to win the World Cup bronze medal

England's goal-laden display and Saka's performance will only add further frustration and regret over Wednesday's semi-final loss to Argentina, where the Arsenal winger was an unused substitute and revealed after the win over France that he "would have loved to have played more".

Tuchel's name was booed by England fans before kick-off, but smiles and cheers at full-time will give the German hope he can lead them to glory at their home Euros in 2028, where France are set to be led by Zinedine Zidane.

Asked about the criticism in his post-match press conference, Tuchel said it "felt as if we went out in group stage without a win," before adding: "It is the first medal in 60 years, the best World Cup on foreign soil, so I hope the players can be proud of that in some time."

'The most ridiculous game ever'

Image: England have achieved their best World Cup finish since 1966

Sky Sports News' Rob Dorsett in Miami:

"Who said these bronze medal matches were a waste of time? That was one of the most ridiculous, exciting, open and thrilling games I can ever remember for an England team.

"Of course, there was a huge sense of unreality about it, with 10 goals in a game that looked dead at half-time when England had a 4-0 lead.

"When France started coming back in the second half, there was panic in the England ranks and a sinking feeling, just three days after the lowest of the lows. But credit England's resilience once more and their sheer guts; they ground this one out when the muscle memory must have been saying terrible things to them.

"Mbappe and Olise were running riot by then. But even those two were eclipsed by Saka.

"The Arsenal man becomes only the fourth Englishman ever to score a World Cup hat-trick, and England scored six! That they conceded four, we can discuss another day. Thomas Tuchel didn't park the bus, and it led to a glorious basketball game.

"It is an extraordinary way for England to end their World Cup, one now with the highest finish since 1966.

"Of course, it will anger many - rightly - that Saka and Marcus Rashford were outstanding against France when they were ignored in the semi-final. Of course, the damnation of Tuchel's tactics when it really mattered still stands.

"But let's just enjoy this one, eh? It was a fantastic, rollercoaster ride, where England just about managed to stay in their seats as we looped-the-loop."

Tuchel explains Saka's Argentina omission as he praises 'special' bronze finish

Image: England collect their bronze medals at the World Cup

England head coach Thomas Tuchel speaking to BBC Sport over Saka's omission in the semi-final loss to Argentina:

"He did everything right. I had just a feeling in the semi-final for Morgan Rogers that he would be involved in something special. That was it. The game itself was so in demand that we were forced into changes because of cramps and the flow of the game.

"Bukayo showed he was a key player; that was never a doubt. I was not even aware he had a hat-trick. I lost the overview of the goalscorers."

On the bronze medal win: "It was like four matches - what happened here. Crazy first half and a turbulent second half. You could see the difference what one day makes.

"We were so, so tired and drained from the last few weeks. Massive compliment and respect for the mentality we showed with all the adversity. Absolutely brilliant.

"I was afraid of the physical demand of the match due to the threat of France. They have far less of a schedule for them; it was less demanding. They had one day more after the semi-final and had less travel distances than us.

"This sums it up for us. We played in the heat in extra time, at altitude. I was worried physically. You can see it in the second half, all the cramps and tiredness.

"But I was never worried about the tiredness. This team has created something special. They showed it again."

Image: Bukayo Saka celebrates scoring his hat-trick

Asked whether he could have played more at the tournament, Bukayo Saka told BBC Sport:

"Of course, I would love to have played more. But of course, it's not the time to talk about that. I try to do my talking on the pitch. It's done now. Move on."

On his fitness: "Yeah, I'm fit. I'm fit."

On the noise around Tuchel: "It's part of the game. When you lose, there's always going to be noise. When you win, there's always going to be noise. It's how you react to it and use it as fuel. Today we had to finish strong."

England assistant Barry's 'emotional' half-time interview

England assistant head coach Anthony Barry speaking to BBC Sport at half-time:

"Have to be honest, there's no frustration [they could not perform like this against Argentina]. I'm a little bit emotional, I can't find the words about how proud I am of those players. We're playing a game with broken hearts, 11 lads with broken hearts.

"I've seen them in the hotel in the last few days with broken hearts. They can build a performance like that by playing through pride for England. The team spirit we've built in the last seven weeks.

"The cynics will say it's too late, but we still play against a world-class opponent and I'm so proud of the boys."

How 10-goal thriller unfolded...

3: ENGLAND GOAL! Rice latches onto a misplaced pass to produce a stunning finish.

18: ENGLAND GOAL! Rice turns provider as his corner is headed in by Konsa

37: ENGLAND GOAL! Saka rebounds home from Rashford's one-on-one chance.

45+2: ENGLAND GOAL! Saka collects Eze's through-ball to fire low into the corner and give England a 4-0 half-time lead.

48: FRANCE GOAL! Mbappe pulls one back with a side-footed finish just minutes into the second half.

54: FRANCE GOAL! Mbappe sets up Barcola, who hammers past Henderson at his near post.

66: FRANCE GOAL! Mbappe becomes the all-time leading World Cup scorer with a brilliant finish after a fine one-two with Olise.

87: ENGLAND GOAL! Saka scores from the spot as he sends the goalkeeper the wrong way.

90+6: FRANCE GOAL! Another twist as Dembele cuts in on his left foot and curls one into the corner.

90+8: ENGLAND GOAL! Bellingham seals the win as he dribbles into the area and rounds the defenders to finish from close range.

Sports.title: England tournament player ratings: Who impressed and who struggled?
Sports.content:
England's World Cup campaign is officially over and while history has been made - it's not quite the history the Three Lions wanted.

A stunning 6-4 win over France in the third-place play-off earned Thomas Tuchel's side a bronze medal - and England's best performance at a World Cup since the 1966 World Cup.

But it could have been more. England were leading their semi-final with Argentina with five minutes of normal time remaining before conceding twice to the holders and exiting in agonising fashion.

So who stepped up for England this summer? Who failed to convince? All of the 26 players, plus Thomas Tuchel, are rated below...

Jordan Pickford - 6

Not a vintage tournament after recent penalty shoot-out successes in previous tournaments. Not great in DR Congo and Norway goals in the knockout stages but did have very good outings against Mexico at the Azteca and then Argentina before the two late goals. Not to blame for England's exit.

Image: Jordan Pickford stood out in his performance against Mexico

Ezri Konsa - 6

The only England player to start every game before the semi-final. Looked pretty good but then clearly ran out of steam during the quarter-finals, which cost him his spot against Argentina. Was back up to speed against France and got a goal out of it - his defensive partnership with Marc Guehi can grow for England.

Image: England's Ezri Konsa was a regular at the back and looked promising

Nico O'Reilly - 6

For a first tournament, absolutely fine. Didn't really put in a standout display in the tournament but got into good areas and didn't make any real mistakes at the back. Couple of fiery moments of frustration and may have been upended by Djed Spence come the end of the tournament. But promising signs.

Image: Nico O'Reilly had a solid first tournament with England

Declan Rice - 7

Rice clearly wasn't at 100 per cent for this tournament. He had a standout moment with his opener in the third-place play-off, but still delivered so many tackles, ball recoveries and strides forward. Crucial in the opening goals against Mexico and Argentina.

After coming off at half-time with illness against Norway, England's vulnerability in midfield showed what happens when he's not there, while his right-back cameo against DR Congo helped change the game.

Image: Rice wasn't fully fit but still delivered

John Stones - 7

Doesn't have a club but can still do a job, even though he came in and out of the team. Had one crucial block in the dying moments against Mexico and did really well to keep Erling Haaland quiet against Norway.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the hilarious moment John Stones pranked England boss Thomas Tuchel with a fake shoulder injury during the dressing room celebrations after beating Mexico. X credit: @England

Marc Guehi - 6

Solid tournament. Went under the radar, which is what you want as a defender. Put his head where it hurts in crucial moments and was particularly important at the Azteca.

Image: England's Marc Guehi put his body on the line at times

Bukayo Saka - 7

Perhaps the most frustrating England player at this tournament, in the most positive sense. Just like in the Champions League final for Arsenal, he clearly wasn't fit enough for most of the summer. Good against Mexico and Norway and got three assists in his first 192 minutes.

Then, when England's hopes of reaching the final were over, he put in an outstanding individual display with a hat-trick against France. He should have started against Argentina, but Tuchel made a huge blunder. Hopefully, come Euro 2028, he will be fully fit.

Image: The stats that show Bukayo Saka should have started at the World Cup

Elliot Anderson - 7

Became a £116m player during the tournament, and while it wasn't quite that level, there were still some really good moments that show a lot of promise. Was better at high pressing - that second goal against Mexico the standout moment - than actually protecting the back four. But if this is his first tournament, Euro 2028 after two years with Man City should be excellent.

Image: Elliot Anderson impressed in his first England tournament

Harry Kane - 7

Before the Norway game, the England captain had a much higher rating. Kane completely went missing in the two biggest games against Norway and Argentina. Still one of the best goalscorers in the world, but how long does he have on the international stage?

Image: England's Harry Kane was in the goals but went missing come the end of the tournament

Jude Bellingham - 8

England's star. Clutch player. And now record breaker - his seven goals are the most by an England player at any major tournament.

It was not just the goals, but his drive to take England up the pitch, which ended up being quite important given how they were eliminated.

Image: Jude Bellingham was England's star player

Marcus Rashford - 5

Got off to a good start with his goal against Croatia but didn't take his chance when Anthony Gordon dropped off. Looked sharp again against France but his withdrawal at half-time made it look like a cameo rather than a contribution. Gordon has taken his spot in the Barcelona and England team, so where does he go now?

Image: Marcus Rashford failed to take his chance

Trevoh Chalobah - n/a

Picked up the phone to Tuchel as the late call-up. But it should have been Trent Alexander-Arnold. Or an actual right-back. Any right-back. Got five minutes at the end of the third-place play-off.

Dean Henderson - 6

Only got a run-out when England lost the semi-final and actually made some decent first-half saves in the third-place play-off against France. Nothing could have been done about France's four in the second half. Could be in a position to challenge Pickford in the future.

Kobbie Mainoo - n/a

A conundrum. Not used despite Rice's fitness woes and England's midfield struggles. Then gets 'injured' for the England reserve game against France after looking 'demoralised'. Not a great look after a resurgence in 2026.

Jordan Henderson - n/a

Six minutes of action against Panama. One yellow card as a substitute against Mexico. One broken wrist in the Azteca celebrations. One of the all-time great cameo stories at the World Cup. There for the dressing room, but had more of an impact than Mainoo. Just.

Image: Jordan Henderson broke his arm in the celebrations against Mexico

Dan Burn - 7

Cult hero. Three big headers in this tournament. Two that crossed the half-way line from inside his own box against Mexico. One smashing one in the final seconds against Norway. Had a simple task and mostly delivered.

Image: Dan Burn became a cult hero

Morgan Rogers - 6

Some nice moments at times, including that assist for Anthony Gordon in the semi-final against Argentina and his long-range effort which forced the Jude Bellingham winner against Norway. But he came into the summer in a No 10 battle with Bellingham and was emphatically beaten. Not his fault, but not his tournament.

Image: Morgan Rogers had limited chances to prove himself

Anthony Gordon - 7

He'll always have that goal against Argentina. A slow start to the tournament but Barcelona's new man really hit top gear in the knockout rounds. Won a penalty in Mexico, England's joint-best starting forward against Norway and scored in the semi-final.

Image: Anthony Gordon made the left wing his own

Ollie Watkins - 5

Did so well to make the plane with his end-of-season form for Aston Villa, but clearly didn't do enough in front of Tuchel in training to impact the actual tournament. Got just seven minutes before the semi-final exit - and became third-choice striker behind Ivan Toney.

Noni Madueke - 5

Image: Noni Madueke failed to take most of the chances presented to him

Played more minutes than he would have expected, but his stock still went down. Got into good areas and his team-mates clearly trusted him, but the final ball wasn't there enough. Barely did anything of note after winning a penalty in the opening minutes against Croatia.

Eberechi Eze - 6

Mostly a substitute this tournament but struggled to make an impact. His excellent outing against France - his only start - showcased what you could get from him in longer periods. But with Gordon and Bellingham impressing, there was no space for a starting spot.

Ivan Toney - 5

Was picked as England's penalty-taker expert and didn't get a penalty chance to prove it. Only got a couple of chaotic minutes against Argentina and did not do much in his only start against France.

James Trafford - n/a

Third-choice goalkeeper. Had a good front row seat of the action though.

Reece James - 6

Everybody knew he'd get injured - and he got injured. Not his fault that England didn't really provide enough back-up for him. Was alright when he played, but cannot be relied on unless his injury record improves.

Djed Spence - 6

That tackle against Argentina was good, wasn't it? Surprised a few this summer with some good displays, including some mazy running in the win over France. His stock has probably gone up a little, especially after his catchy song.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After Djed Spence's brilliant cameo off the bench against Norway, England fans Ben Cipolla and Dan Lucas came up with a new song for the full back titled 'Total Eclipse of Djed Spence'

Jarell Quansah - 5

Image: England's Jarell Quansah was sent off against Mexico

Not a bad right-back option and was unlucky that he couldn't get his two-game suspension in the knockout rounds suspended by a government official. He will learn from the red card against Mexico, but looked slow to the game in his next appearance vs France.

Thomas Tuchel - 6

At the start of the tournament, it was all about Tuchel's excellent in-game changes. The half-time team talk against Croatia, the backs-to-the-wall effort against Mexico. But then the England head coach came up short when it mattered - which is the opposite of what he was brought in to do.

Not starting Saka against Argentina was followed by a defensive outlook to see out the semi-final. It backfired. He is under pressure.

Anthony Barry - 6

For media appearances, 10/10. "We're playing with broken hearts," during half-time of the France win was absolutely golden. He was also the mastermind behind Rice playing at right-back vs DR Congo. But that makes him equally responsible for England's questionable tactical calls.

Sports.title: World Cup 2026: Spain v Argentina final buildup; England win 10-goal thriller – live
Sports.content:
3m ago 15.33 BST Another of our men on the ground… Photograph: Bluesky Share

5m ago 15.31 BST Potential delays to get into the MetLife Stadium Matt Hughes US Secret Service staff are conducting individual body and bag searches of every fan attending the World Cup final leading to concerns that all of the 82,500 ticket holders may not get into the ground before kickoff. Defending champions Argentina’s meeting with Spain at the New York/New Jersey Stadium has been designated as a National Special Security Event due to the attendance of US President Donald Trump, with the highest level of security measures put in place. Share

34m ago 15.02 BST I think it’s also worth noting the extent to which Spanish footballing culture pervades the grass-roots game around the world; along with Ronaldinho, who integrated freestyle trickery and attitude into the elite level, it is the biggest influence on the modern style. Share

46m ago 14.50 BST “A week ago, France were the greatest side ever seen in a World Cup,” says Gary Stover. “Anybody think Hall or Shaw would have been better than Spence? Anybody think Foden or Palmer would have saved England v Argentina? Maybe someone who’s currently having to make things work on the pitch, say Emma Hayes, has a better understanding of today’s game. Born in England, made in the USA, she sees first hand how the attitudes of me first, team second have slowed the development of both.” I don’t think it’s right to say Hayes was made in the USA – she was already an all-timer before she moved. But yes, I agree that Shaw and Hall are both better than the left-backs taken ahead of them. Share

48m ago 14.47 BST I advocated for this before Argentina played England, and they didn’t do it, but can they really afford to take on Spain with a midfield two? I’d get Lautaro into a tight front three with Simeone dropping out, then a narrow trio behind them and the full-backs tasked with supplying width. Share

1h ago 14.29 BST “I’m wary of disagreeing with Emma Hayes,” writes David Wall, “but i think she’s wrong about the importance of individuals to Spain. Spain have been hindered in this tournament because Williams has barely been able to play and Lamine Yamal has been half-fit for a lot of it. The replacements for them are simply not up to their class and impact. Perhaps in terms of creating passing angles and retaining possession it’s not important which individuals are playing as almost all of the Spanish players do that by habit. But it’s just not true to say that particular individuals don’t make a significant difference to how they play and how effective they are.” I don’t think someone who’s managed so many brilliant individuals doesn’t think the best of them can determine the outcome of games.
